questions.text: An object moves 10 m in 2 seconds. Its speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance / Time = 10 / 2 = 5 m/s.

questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only; it has no direction. Velocity and displacement are vectors.

questions.text: A car travelling at 60 km/h comes to rest in 5 seconds. Its retardation is:
questions.explanation: 60 km/h = 16.67 m/s. Retardation = 16.67/5 ≈ 3.33 m/s².

questions.text: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: The area under a v-t graph represents the distance (displacement) covered.

questions.text: An object is said to be in uniform motion when:
options: Its speed changes at regular intervals
It covers equal distances in equal intervals of time
Its direction changes but speed remains constant
questions.explanation: Uniform motion means covering equal distances in equal time intervals.

questions.text: The number of zeroes of a quadratic polynomial is at most:
questions.explanation: A quadratic polynomial has degree 2, so it can have at most 2 zeroes.

questions.text: If α and β are zeroes of p(x) = x² – 5x + 6, then α + β =
questions.explanation: For p(x) = x² – 5x + 6, sum of zeroes = –(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²) = 5.

questions.text: The product of zeroes of x² – 5x + 6 is:
questions.explanation: Product of zeroes = constant term / leading coefficient = 6/1 = 6.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a polynomial?
questions.explanation: x + 1/x = x + x⁻¹ has a negative exponent, so it is not a polynomial.

questions.text: A cubic polynomial can have at most how many zeroes?
questions.explanation: The number of zeroes of a polynomial equals its degree. A cubic has degree 3.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a combination reaction?
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O combines two substances to form one product.

questions.text: The decomposition of CaCO₃ on heating is an example of:
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ breaks one compound into two, so it is a decomposition reaction.

questions.text: Which indicator is used to test for carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: CO₂ turns lime water (Ca(OH)₂) milky, forming CaCO₃ precipitate.

questions.text: In the reaction Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu, which element is oxidized?
questions.explanation: Iron loses electrons (is oxidized) and displaces copper from copper sulphate.

questions.text: What is the balanced form of H₂ + O₂ → H₂O?
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is balanced: 4H and 2O on each side.

questions.text: Which of the following is a rational number?
questions.explanation: 3/4 can be expressed as a ratio of two integers, so it is rational.

questions.text: The additive identity for rational numbers is:
questions.explanation: Adding 0 to any rational number gives the same number. So 0 is the additive identity.

questions.text: What is the multiplicative inverse of 3/5?
questions.explanation: The multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of 3/5 is 5/3 because (3/5) × (5/3) = 1.

questions.text: Rational numbers are closed under which operations?
questions.explanation: Rational numbers are closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication. Division by zero is excluded.

questions.text: Between any two rational numbers, how many rational numbers exist?
questions.explanation: Between any two rational numbers, there are infinitely many rational numbers.
